title: Scorpius Dynamics — Hosting path & p95 throughput workshop

Share SOC2 + ISO documents and private deployment checklist
Schedule on-prem pilot kickoff for week of 2026-05-25
action_items: Leila Chen - prepare benchmark harness + sample configs - due 2026-05-18
Ravi Menon - provide 5 representative prompt sets + token length histograms - due 2026-05-17

summary: Discovery workshop focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency and streaming behavior for Scorpius Dynamics' document summarization product. Customer cares about sub-300ms p95 for single-turn short responses, steady-state token/sec for bursty traffic, and options for hosted vs dedicated vs private with KMS/VPC requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Leila Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Scorpius CTO), Elena Alvarez (Lead ML Eng), Markus He (Infra)
---
[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everybody, thanks for joining, can folks hear me ok?
[00:10] Ravi Menon: yeah we can hear you, thanks Jordan, thanks Leila.
[00:15] Jordan Park: cool, quick agenda: baseline of current infra, target p95 and concurrency, streaming/token throughput profiling, then next steps for a pilot. if we run over we can sync afterwards. sound good?
[00:28] Elena Alvarez: sounds great.
[00:30] Leila Chen: quick intro from our side — I'm Leila, I'm the systems SE that will own the benchmark configs and the performance tuning.
[00:40] Markus He: Markus here, infra. our product is doc-summarize, typical prompt sizes are 70-300 tokens, but we have bursts where many small prompts hit at once.
[00:53] Jordan Park: ok good. can you give a sense of current numbers — p95 today, concurrency, cloud setup?
[01:02] Elena Alvarez: right now we're on a managed inference endpoint in-cloud, p95 around 700ms for short responses, and our peak concurrency observed is about 120 req/s, but that mixes streaming and blocking calls. cost is getting high.
[01:18] Ravi Menon: the hard requirement from product is sub-300ms p95 for short single-turn summaries, ideally 95th percentile under 200ms for <100-token outputs but we know that's ambitious.
[01:33] Leila Chen: ok that's a helpful target. so we typically look at three hosting paths — Redwood Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), or Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). each has different latency/cost characteristics.
[01:47] Jordan Park: just to call out, when you say streaming are you sending chunked tokens to clients or are you waiting for full response?
[01:54] Elena Alvarez: client side needs streaming for the UI, we stream tokens as they arrive. most of our p95 complaints are on initial token latency and tail from concurrency.
[02:06] Leila Chen: ok, two separate constraints then: first-token latency (cold start + routing) and sustained tokens/sec during generation. we'll break those down.
[02:15] [00:02:30] Markus He: also security — private VPC + KMS for keys, SOC2 necessary, maybe ISO.
[02:23] Jordan Park: yes we'll send security pack.
---
[00:03:00] Leila Chen: to align expectations: for a hosted API we can often get p95 ~150-350ms for short outputs on our verified small/medium models with streaming, depending on model and region. Dedicated reduces jitter and secures throughput for sustained high qps; Private removes egress and network hops but you take on infra ops.
[03:22] Elena Alvarez: can you explain the sources of tail latency — is it batching or scheduling?
[03:29] Leila Chen: good question. tail comes from a few places: scheduling (queueing) when GPUs are saturated, kernel warmups for certain layers, KV cache misses for long context, and network/hop latency for hosted paths. for streaming there's also token emission scheduling and pack flush intervals.
[03:48] Ravi Menon: what about KV cache? our use case keeps per-user context ~2k tokens sometimes, will that blow performance?
[03:56] Leila Chen: KV cache size matters for memory but more for throughput; runtime keeps KV in-GPU and reuses it across tokens, but long context increases token compute. for p95 short outputs with long context it's often compute-bound. we can quantize and use optimized kernels; we also suggested prefix caching for templates.
[04:16] [00:04:30] Markus He: any rule-of-thumb for concurrency to reserve? we want to avoid 429s in spikes.
[04:24] Jordan Park: we size pools by token/sec and concurrency; typical approach is measure tokens/sec per model and then compute required GPUs for steady-state plus headroom for bursts. Leila will run a token/sec benchmark against 3 models to give numbers.
---
[00:06:00] Leila Chen: here's what we'll benchmark: 1) small open LM (6B quant) — low latency baseline, 2) medium (13B q4_0) — production-like, 3) large (70B quantized variant) — upper bound. we'll run both streaming and non-streaming scenarios, with prompt lengths 50/200/600 tokens and concurrency shapes: steady 50/s, burst to 300/s for 30s.
[06:26] Elena Alvarez: do you do prefix batching? our app reuses the same system prompt a lot.
[06:31] Leila Chen: yes we have automatic prefix caching and a KV cache policy that avoids re-compute for repeated prefixes. that usually reduces per-token cost and latency for repeated templates. note: prefix caching effectiveness depends on request distribution.
[06:44] Ravi Menon: what's the expected p95 improvement with Dedicated?
[06:48] Leila Chen: Dedicated removes noisy neighbors and gives predictable queueing; in our experience p95 jitter drops by ~25-60% depending on model and request mix. streaming first-token latency improves because routing is local to the dedicated pool.
[07:00] [00:07:30] Markus He: any hardware recs? A100 vs H100?
[07:06] Leila Chen: H100 helps with throughput and larger KV ops; A100 still fine for small/medium models with quantization. Dedicated can be configured on H100 for heavy throughput. we'll include kernel-level throughput numbers in the benchmark report.
---
[00:08:00] Elena Alvarez: curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated is saturated can traffic fallback to Hosted?
[08:08] Jordan Park: yes, smart routing supports fallback to hosted or a cheaper model variant; policies are configurable per-route. fallbacks preserve availability at cost of potential quality shift.
[08:19] Ravi Menon: that helps. about streaming — we need sub-100ms between first token and subsequent token streams, otherwise UX looks choppy. is that realistic?
[08:29] Leila Chen: per-token spacing is usually <20-40ms for short tokens if the model computes quickly; network buffering and flush intervals can add to that. we'll tweak chunk sizes and flush windows in the runtime.
---
[00:09:30] Leila Chen: quick note on metrics — we'll collect p95, p99, cold-start, happy-path first-byte, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token. also trace spans so you can see where tail is coming from.
[09:42] Markus He: tracing — will that work in Private? we need audit logs retained 2 years.
[09:49] Jordan Park: yes private offers audit logs retention options and KMS integration; long retention is an add-on. we'll include the compliance worksheet.
---
[00:11:00] Leila Chen: ok practical next step: we'll need your sample prompts and token histograms, plus a production-ish traffic file (a minute-level arrival file) so our harness can replay traffic for burst tests.
[11:14] Elena Alvarez: we can extract that from prod, we have a 30 day trace.
[11:20] Ravi Menon: also want to see cost tradeoffs — for example Dedicated reserved vs Hosted over expected QPS and token volume.
[11:27] Jordan Park: we'll produce a simple cost model: tokens/sec * seconds * price_per_token or GPU-hours for Dedicated; we'll provide ballpark.
---
[00:12:30] Leila Chen: small gotcha — streaming benchmarks can look better if you only measure per-token throughput; p95 interactive latency needs to be measured at the client-level. we'll set up both server-side and client-side probes.
[12:49] Markus He: makes sense. for the pilot we want to run in our EU region, can Redwood host there?
[12:56] Jordan Park: yes we have EU regions; we'll deploy the benchmark in the EU region to match latency.
---
[00:14:00] Elena Alvarez: question about quantization/accuracy: will q4_0 or q2 make our summaries worse?
[14:06] Leila Chen: sometimes quantization affects quality; we'll include quality checks with your prompts in the benchmark so you can see ROUGE/BLEU or human-snippets. also can suggest hybrid approach — CPU fallbacks for particular ranking steps.
[14:22] Ravi Menon: for us latency matters more than tiny quality drops; threshold is, quality must remain acceptable to product.
[14:29] Leila Chen: understood, we'll include quality delta metrics.
---
[00:15:30] Jordan Park: I want to flag one engineering detail — KV cache eviction policies during large fanouts can increase tail. Leila maybe you can add cache warmup in the harness.
[15:42] Leila Chen: yep, we'll include warmup sequences and measure cold vs warm p95.
---
[00:16:30] Elena Alvarez: can we talk about rate-limiting? we want graceful degradation not hard 429s.
[16:37] Leila Chen: policies support token-based throttles, adaptive queuing, and auto-fallback to smaller model variants. you can set soft and hard limits and we can send back 202s with async tokens if you prefer orchestration.
[16:56] Markus He: async would be useful for some background reports.
---
[00:18:00] Leila Chen: we'll include an A/B idea: keep a fast small model for the first-streamed token and then patch with a higher-quality model for final pass for edge cases. it adds complexity but can help latency.
[18:22] Ravi Menon: do you have customers using that pattern?
[18:26] Leila Chen: yes a few. it's sometimes called a split-pass or two-tier inference.
---
[00:19:30] Jordan Park: ok let's capture explicit success criteria — Elena?
[19:35] Elena Alvarez: success = p95 < 300ms for 90% of short (<100 token) queries, sustained tokens/sec to support peak of 300 req/s (with average ~150 tokens), streaming first-token under 150ms and per-token spacing <50ms, and no data leaves our VPC for Private option.
[19:56] Leila Chen: that's clear — we'll aim benchmarks at that.
---
[00:20:30] Leila Chen: operational constraints? SLOs, SLAs, budget?
[20:36] Ravi Menon: budget is the other side — we want cost roughly equal to current but lower jitter. if Dedicated is required we'll need commitment but prefer pilot first.
[20:48] Jordan Park: pilot can run on a smaller Dedicated pool or hosted with capacity reservation for a short window.
---
[00:22:00] Leila Chen: I'm going to summarize the benchmark outputs we'll deliver: 1) p95/p99 first-byte latency for streaming and non-streaming, 2) tokens/sec steady and burst graphs, 3) cost-per-token/estimated monthly spend across hosting modes, 4) quality deltas vs your golden prompts, 5) tracing breakdowns showing queue vs compute vs network.
[22:31] Elena Alvarez: perfect.
---
[00:23:00] Markus He: about security docs, can you share how KMS integration works and whether keys leave our control?
[23:07] Jordan Park: with Private we integrate your KMS/HSM and keys do not leave your control; hosted supports customer-managed key options via cloud KMS but there are export rules, we'll send specifics.
[23:20] Ravi Menon: retention windows for logs — we need two years.
[23:24] Jordan Park: we'll propose a retention addon.
---
[00:24:30] Leila Chen: ok on benchmarks: do you want us to test both with and without prefix caching enabled?
[24:36] Elena Alvarez: yes please. prefix caching might be the main lever.
[24:40] Leila Chen: noted.
---
[00:25:00] Jordan Park: any regulatory constraints re: data residency?
[25:05] Elena Alvarez: EU-only, no cross-region copying.
[25:08] Jordan Park: we'll keep benchmarks and pilot in EU.
---
[00:26:30] Leila Chen: quick note on metrics collection — we'll give you a spreadsheet with token/sec and latency percentiles, and a prometheus export if you want to pull into your dashboards.
[26:42] Markus He: good.
---
[00:28:00] Ravi Menon: do you support SAML SSO for console?
[28:05] Jordan Park: yes SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
---
[00:29:00] Elena Alvarez: any unusual caveats we should be aware of?
[29:05] Leila Chen: sometimes model library mismatches happen between quantized variants and reference; we'll lock model commits during pilot to ensure reproducibility. also kernel selection can change performance across minor runtime updates.
---
[00:30:30] Jordan Park: ok going to recap actionables and timeline.
[30:35] Jordan Park: 1) Scorpius sends prompts + token histograms + region preference by 2026-05-17.
[30:44] Elena Alvarez: yes we'll get that.
[30:47] Jordan Park: 2) Redwood will run multi-model benchmarks and return a report by 2026-05-21.
[30:55] Leila Chen: 3) we'll include an EU pilot config and pricing ballpark by 2026-05-15.
[31:04] Jordan Park: 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-05-25 if all aligns.
---
[00:32:00] Markus He: anything else?
[32:03] Elena Alvarez: one last question — can we simulate real user sessions with interleaved long and short contexts?
[32:10] Leila Chen: yes the harness supports mixed session replay. we'll need your trace.
---
[00:33:00] Jordan Park: ok great, I'll send the SOC2 and the private deployment checklist after the call.
[33:06] Ravi Menon: thanks, and please include sample configs for the three models.
[33:10] Leila Chen: will do.
---
[00:34:30] Jordan Park: quick notes on benchmarking methodology: we prefer real-client replay and also synthetic fanout to push the tail; we record server-side traces and client-side jitter so we can pinpoint root cause.
[34:47] Elena Alvarez: that's valuable.
---
[00:36:00] Leila Chen: small aside — if you end up private onprem, our on-prem package includes a monitoring agent and an ops-runbook for kernel upgrades.
[36:12] Markus He: ops-runbook is a must.
---
[00:37:30] Jordan Park: time check — we have about 15 mins left.
[37:33] Ravi Menon: ok go ahead.
---
[00:38:00] Leila Chen: we'll also log per-token emission timing to make sure streaming is smooth; that helps tune flush windows.
[38:09] Elena Alvarez: do you have default flush window?
[38:13] Leila Chen: default is 50ms but we can tune down to 20ms on dedicated infra.
---
[00:39:30] Markus He: curious — how do you measure tokens/sec for multi-turn chats vs single-turn?
[39:39] Leila Chen: we measure generated tokens per second across the whole session and normalize by request; multi-turn mostly affects KV cache; we report both per-request token/sec and aggregate token/sec.
---
[00:41:00] Jordan Park: moving to close — any blockers?
41:05 Elena Alvarez: none, just need the benchmark and security docs.
[41:09] Ravi Menon: same.
---
[00:42:00] Jordan Park: ok we'll get the deliverables: benchmark configs, results, pricing ballpark, security pack.
[42:10] Leila Chen: I'll follow up with the harness repo link and how to run it locally. expect the report by 5/21.
[42:20] Markus He: thanks.
---
[00:43:00] Jordan Park: final recap and next steps — I've logged action items in crm, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for pilot kickoff tentative week of 5/25.
[43:12] Elena Alvarez: perfect. thanks all.
[43:15] Ravi Menon: thanks, bye.
[43:18] Jordan Park: thanks everyone, bye.
